---
title: "Distance circle crossings"
description: "How OPDI finds the crossings of circles of 40, 50, 60, 100, 110 and 120 NM around the departure and destination airports (xing-{radius}nm), and the circle columns of the flight list."
---

## In one sentence

An `xing-{radius}nm` event marks each moment a flight crosses a circle of
fixed radius (40, 50, 60, 100, 110 or 120 NM) around its own departure or
destination airport.

## What it needs

- The departure and destination airports of the flight list, after the
  correction by runway events (see
  [Departure and destination airports](airports.qmd)), and their positions
  from OurAirports. Circles are drawn only around these two airports.
- The cleaned positions of the track's reports.

## How it is computed

1. For each report with a position, compute the great-circle distance to the
   departure airport and to the destination airport.
2. **Dead band.** A track running along a circle would cross it many times. A
   band of 1 NM on each side is used: the aircraft counts as outside the 40 NM
   circle only once it is more than 41 NM away, and inside only once it is
   less than 39 NM away. A crossing is the moment the side changes.
3. **Interpolation.** The time, position and measurements of the crossing are
   interpolated in a straight line between the two reports either side of the
   circle itself. Reports without a position are skipped. When the two
   reports are more than 30 minutes apart, no crossing is given. A report
   without an altitude takes its last known altitude, at most 30 s old.
4. **Position jumps.** A position that jumps away from the track and back
   (one or two reports whose steps to their neighbours imply more than
   1,000 kt, with 2 NM of tolerance) is treated as missing. A crossing whose
   two reports still imply more than 1,000 kt is not given, unless no other
   circle lies between the two distances: the position then stepped and stayed
   (as near areas of GPS spoofing), and the crossing is kept with
   `info.position_jump` = true.
5. The bearing of the crossing point is computed from the airport.
6. Every crossing is kept and numbered in time order.

The flight list takes, for each radius, the first outbound crossing around
the departure airport after the take-off (`c40_dep` to `c120_dep`) and the
last inbound crossing around the destination airport before the landing
(`c40_arr` to `c120_arr`). When the take-off or landing time is unknown, that
time limit is not applied.

## Based on

- The circles are those of ICAO's indicators ([GANP KPI
  overview](../resources.qmd#ref-ganp-kpi)): KPI08, additional time in terminal airspace,
  measures from a 40 NM cylinder around the destination airport, with a
  100 NM variant for airports where aircraft hold further out; KPI05, actual
  en-route extension, starts and ends en-route airspace at the same
  cylinders.
- The crossing method (dead band, interpolation) was developed for OPDI and
  is the same as for the [flight-level crossings](flight-level-crossings.qmd).

## What is published

Event types `xing-40nm`, `xing-50nm`, `xing-60nm`, `xing-100nm`,
`xing-110nm` and `xing-120nm` (the family `xing-{radius}nm`), with position,
altitude, `distance_flown_nm` and `time_passed_s`. Their `info` holds
`apt_icao`, `direction` (`inbound` or `outbound`), `crossing_seq`, `bearing`,
`flight_level`, `bracket_s` and, where it applies, `position_jump` (see the
[Data dictionary](../data/dictionary.qmd#info-fields)).

Flight list columns `c40_arr`, `c50_arr`, `c60_arr`, `c100_arr`, `c110_arr`,
`c120_arr`, `c40_dep`, `c50_dep`, `c60_dep`, `c100_dep`, `c110_dep` and
`c120_dep` (UTC).

## Use cases

- **Additional time in the terminal area**: `aldt` minus `c40_arr` (or
  `c100_arr`), compared with an unimpeded time per entry sector
  (`info.bearing`).
- **Where arrivals come from**: the bearing of the inbound crossings around
  an airport, per hour.
- **Departure climb-out**: the time from `atot` to `c40_dep`.

## Limitations

The circles are drawn only around the two airports of the flight-list row,
so on a track holding several flights the middle stop has none. See
[Limitations: distance circles](../limitations.qmd#lim-rings).
